candidates.exact_span:
permittee must collect an effluent composite sample volume during the period of
   discharge that is sufficient to complete the required toxicity tests with daily renewal of
   effluent, and must meet the holding time between collection and first use of the sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a toxicity-monitoring obligation applies hinges on interpreting 'during the period of discharge,' the sufficiency of composite volume for required tests, and holding-time compliance; different readings change which requirements are deemed applicable for a given monitoring period.

candidates.exact_span:
When possible, the effluent samples used for the toxicity tests shall be collected on
   separate days.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The conditional 'when possible' and the separate-day collection rule affect whether separate-day sampling was required versus excused; for B this changes applicable monitoring obligations, and for C it affects whether absent separate-day samples reflect a documented no-data/exception state or missing required evidence.

candidates.exact_span:
The effluent composite sample collection duration and the static renewal
   protocol associated with the abbreviated sample collection must be documented in the
   full report required in Item 3 of this section.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Documentation of collection duration and abbreviated static-renewal protocol is itself a reporting obligation tied to Item 3; whether that documentation exists or satisfies the requirement changes B applicability assessments and C classification of missing versus adequately documented evidence.

candidates.exact_span:
**Test failure may not be construed or reported as invalid due to a coefficient of
   variation value of greater than 40%, or a PMSD value greater than the higher value on the
   range provided.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This clause governs when elevated CV or PMSD values may invalidate a toxicity test result; different interpretations of 'may not be construed or reported as invalid' change whether a reported test failure remains an enforceable exceedance comparison or is excluded from numeric compliance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span:
The statistical analyses used to determine if there is a significant difference between the
   control and the critical dilution shall be in accordance with the methods for determining
   the No Observed Effect Concentration (NOEC) as described in the appropriate method
   manual listed in Part II or the most recent update thereof.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The mandated NOEC statistical method and reference to Part II manuals determine how pass/fail against toxicity limits is computed for A, and which analytical procedure is required for B; ambiguity over 'appropriate method manual' or 'most recent update' could change both the applicable limit comparison and the monitoring method obligation.

candidates.exact_span:
1) Dilution water used in the toxicity tests will be receiving water collected as close
          to the point of discharge as possible but unaffected by the discharge. The
          permittee shall substitute synthetic dilution water of similar pH, hardness, and
          alkalinity to the closest downstream perennial water for;
               i. toxicity tests conducted on effluent discharges to receiving water
                  classified as intermittent streams; and
              ii. toxicity tests conducted on effluent discharges where no receiving water is
                  available due to zero flow conditions.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Default receiving-water versus mandatory synthetic dilution water depends on stream classification and zero-flow conditions; interpreting 'intermittent streams,' 'zero flow conditions,' or 'unaffected by the discharge' changes which monitoring protocol was required (B) and whether a period reflects conditional non-requirement or unresolved evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span:
2) If the receiving water is unsatisfactory as a result of instream toxicity (fails to
          fulfill the test acceptance criteria), the permittee may substitute synthetic dilution
          water for the receiving water in all subsequent tests provided the unacceptable
          receiving water test met the following stipulations:
                i. a synthetic dilution water control which fulfills the test acceptance require-
                   ments was run concurrently with the receiving water control;
               ii. the test indicating receiving water toxicity has been carried out to
                   completion,
              iii. the permittee includes all test results indicating receiving water toxicity
                   with the full report and information required; and
              iv. the synthetic dilution water shall have a pH, hardness, and alkalinity
                   similar to that of the receiving water or closest downstream perennial
                   water not adversely affected by the discharge, provided the magnitude of
                   these parameters will not cause toxicity in the synthetic dilution water.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Substitution after instream-toxicity failure is permissive ('may substitute') and conditioned on concurrent controls, completed tests, reporting, and water-quality similarity; different readings of whether those stipulations were met change the valid test protocol (B), whether resulting toxicity results are enforceable for limit comparison (A), and whether missing reports or incomplete tests are documented exceptions versus inadequate evidence (C).
